The results answer the objective. On the noisy 'concepts' labels, 176 of the 214 assessable concepts are reliably predictable (test median AUROC 0.940, CV 0.943). All 17 assessable manual concepts are reliable (AUROC 0.996). Leakage gaps are negligible (≤0.0005), so the grouped and duplicate-aware design holds. The data-quality audit is thorough: severe imbalance (Gini 0.81, 1726 of 1947 labels below support), 8.5% of images in near-duplicate clusters (28% of clusters cross splits, 6.4% of test images have a training duplicate), label precision of 0.937 against manual labels, and 20% of positive labels with no support in their caption. Points to note in the report: the encoder's zero-shot recall@10 of 0.955 may mean the images overlap its pretraining data. The two duplicate-detection methods agree poorly (Jaccard 0.027). The image-caption check was not cross-fitted, and the map's stability (0.53) only just passes. None of these is a strong enough reason to revise.
